title: USMF Version 6.0: Quantum-Geometry, Matter, and Radiation All in One Expansion Law
abstract: This model explains the Universe’s expansion without dark energy or exotic particles.  Instead, all distances and times slowly shrink due to quantum-geometric effects.  A single analytic formula for H(z) then combines three physical contributions—quantum-shrinkage, ordinary clustering, and photon pressure—under one square root.  It reproduces the exact (1+z)^4 scaling at early times, the (1+z)^3 era of structure growth, and the observed late-time acceleration, matching supernova, BAO, and CMB data to ΛCDM precision.
description:
USMFv6.0 uses one master equation for the Hubble rate:

  H(z) = H_A * sqrt(
    (1+z)^(2*p_alpha) * (1 + k_exp*(1+z)^(s_exp))
    + \Omega_{m eff}*(1+z)^3
    + \Omega_{\gamma}*(1+z)^4
  )

• **H_A** sets the present-day Hubble scale (km/s/Mpc).
• **Quantum-geometry term** (first line) controls late-time acceleration via exponent p_alpha and shape parameters k_exp, s_exp.
• **Matter-like term** \Omega_{m eff}*(1+z)^3 reproduces structure growth and BAO amplitude without new particles.
• **Radiation term** \Omega_{\gamma}*(1+z)^4 enforces the exact early-Universe behaviour.
• **\Omega_{\gamma}** (photon density), **\Omega_b** (baryon density), and **z_{m rec}** are fixed to observed values; **\Omega_b** obeys BBN constraints.
• The sound horizon r_s is computed automatically by integrating c/H(z) up to z_{m rec}.

With just twelve fit parameters, this single law matches Type Ia supernova distances, BAO scales, and the Planck CMB power spectra at the same level as ΛCDM—no “Λ” or dark-matter particles needed.
